summary: Root cause identified: the order-service deployment dep-5101 (v2.14.0, live 2026-03-03T12:10:00Z) added a new MarginCheckValidator to the validation chain and removed the legacy OrderRules.validateMargin(); the new validator dereferences a null marginProfile for F&O (derivatives) orders, throwing java.lang.NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 and returning HTTP 500. Confidence is medium (H1 = 0.74, capped by the Critic after two review rounds), well ahead of the residual alternatives (H2 0.08, H3 0.06, H4 0.02 rejected). The causal chain is tight: dep-5101 is the only change to any component in the window, the error onset (12:10–12:12Z bucket, first error 12:12:31Z) follows it immediately, and all 426 ERROR logs in the window are NullPointerException/FNO marginProfile-null with zero equity-order failures. No downstream, shared-dependency, or capacity signal co-precides the onset; order-service is the only service that steps up in error rate. Mitigation is to revert or roll back dep-5101.

ranked_hypotheses.title: dep-5101 in order-service: new MarginCheckValidator mishandles null marginProfile for F&O orders
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The v2.14.0 deployment dep-5101 to order-service (12:10:00Z) added a new MarginCheckValidator into the validation chain and removed the legacy OrderRules.validateMargin(). The new validator dereferences the margin profile it retrieves without a null guard, and for F&O (derivatives) orders that profile is absent, so validation throws java.lang.NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 and the request fails with HTTP 500. The fault originates in the order-service code change itself; whether the null profile comes from a missing data record or from the new code failing to populate it is one and the same origin (the new validation path) and is noted as an open detail.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5101 deploys order-service v2.14.0 at 12:10:00Z, adding new MarginCheckValidator and removing legacy OrderRules.validateMargin()

This is the only deployment across the entire fleet in the 11:00-13:59Z window; the only config change is unrelated (notification-service email.batch_size), and the standard deploy/config feeds are empty for ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka, portfolio-service

Error onset falls in the 12:10Z bucket, error rate stepping from 0.22% baseline to 14.74% at 12:10Z and holding ~18.3-18.8%, with the first error log at 12:12:31Z — immediately after the deployment goes live

The new validation path runs strictly on the derivatives (F&O) path; every one of the 426 ERROR logs is an NPE at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 with orderType=FNO or 'marginProfile is null for account', and zero equity/non-FNO error logs exist

The null dereference throws an immediate application exception rather than a latency/resource symptom: latency_p99 flat ~150ms, cpu_pct flat ~40%, db_pool_in_use flat ~14, memory flat ~60%, ledger-db connections flat ~62
Only order-service shows an error step; pricing-engine, exchange-gateway, payment-service, portfolio-service and ledger-db all stay flat at ~0.2% error rate with no step at the 12:10-12:12Z onset
The api-gateway's smaller concurrent error increase is the same 5xx response surfacing at the caller, not an independent fault

assumptions: The 'marginProfile is null' condition is produced by the new code path itself (missing/incorrect handling of F&O accounts) rather than by a broken external data source that the new code merely exposed; the null's provenance is not directly traced.
No rollback was performed during the window, so no recovery evidence exists for or against this hypothesis.

The deploy/config feeds can be trusted as complete for shared datastores — the dependency agent flagged that infra-level changes might not surface there, though they did return the empty result for the named components.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Unseen marginProfile data source degrading, with dep-5101 only exposing the gap
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The NPE is a symptom rather than the fault: the component that owns or computes margin profiles for accounts degraded or returned incomplete data, so marginProfile was null. The dep-5101 change is at most the event that revealed a pre-existing data gap, and the fix would lie outside order-service in that data source.
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: unidentified margin/portfolio profile source (candidate: portfolio-service, or a margin datastore)

causal_chain.claim: Some margin/portfolio profile source stops returning valid marginProfile for F&O accounts at ~12:10-12:12Z
order-service's newly active MarginCheckValidator dereferences the missing value
NPE at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 surfaces as HTTP 500 on derivatives orders

assumptions: An unidentified margin/profile source exists and was degraded at exactly the onset.

Its degradation is invisible in error_rate, latency, logs and resource metrics because it returns null without erroring — this is unfalsifiable with the available tools since no null-return/data-completeness metric exists.
The onset's coincidence with dep-5101 within one to two minutes is accidental.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Silent change or degradation on a shared component (ledger-db / redis-cache / kafka) invisible to the standard feeds
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared component on order-service's dependency graph degraded or received an infra-level change that does not surface in the service-scoped deploy/config endpoints — e.g. ledger-db IOPS throttling, redis-cache saturation, or a kafka change — causing the derivatives order path to fail with 500s. This follows the HIST-110 (ledger-db statement timeouts) and HIST-115 (order-service pool misconfiguration) precedents.

causal_chain.claim: A shared dependency degrades or is changed but is invisible in the service-scoped deploy/config history
order-service's order path (especially derivatives) begins failing as a result
Failures surface as HTTP 500 on POST /v1/orders

assumptions: The shared component's degradation is real but unmeasured: slow_queries_per_min for ledger-db, redis hit_ratio/memory/evictions and kafka metrics were never retrieved (budget exhausted).
The precise one-to-two-minute coincidence with dep-5101 is accidental.
The failure mechanism would still have to produce an immediate NPE inside a brand-new validator, which no shared-infra degradation explains directly.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Capacity/resource saturation in order-service on the derivatives path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A traffic or load surge on the derivatives path saturated order-service resources (DB pool, thread pool, CPU), producing 500s — consistent with the HIST-115 precedent of connection-pool exhaustion.

causal_chain.claim: Derivatives order volume rises and saturates a pooled resource in order-service

assumptions: A load surge occurred but was not observable in the queried metrics (now positively refuted by F36).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Resource metrics directly refute saturation: latency_p99 flat ~150ms, cpu_pct flat ~40% (F11), db_pool_in_use flat ~14 max 15.22, memory flat ~60% (F18), and ledger-db connections_active flat ~62 (F17). Request volume is flat at ~230-235 req/s across the whole incident (F36), so there is no traffic surge either. The errors are immediate NullPointerExceptions in a specific validator (F9), not pool/timeout errors.

facts.statement: order-service was deployed to v2.14.0 (dep-5101) at 2026-03-03T12:10:00Z, 12 minutes before the reported onset; the deployment is still live with no rollback. Its summary is 'Refactor order validation; add margin check for F&O orders', with changes 'new MarginCheckValidator in validation chain' and 'remove legacy OrderRules.validateMargin()'.
A fleet-wide deployment query (all services, 10:00–13:59Z) returned exactly one deployment: dep-5101 on order-service. No other service deployed in the window.
The only config change across all services in the window is cfg-2101 on notification-service (email.batch_size 200 -> 250 at 11:21:00Z), unrelated to order placement or derivatives orders.
order-service's downstream HTTP callees on the derivatives path (pricing-engine, exchange-gateway) had zero deployments in the window, so neither can explain the onset via a code release.

order-service error rate jumped from a baseline of ~0.17–0.29% to ~18.5% between the 12:09Z and 12:12Z buckets; the first elevated bucket averaged 18.51% and errors are present continuously thereafter.

All 426 order-service ERROR logs in the window are NullPointerException in MarginCheckValidator.validate at MarginCheckValidator.java:88, and every stack-trace line reads orderType=FNO (derivatives); the two patterns are 'NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate' (224) and 'order rejected with 500: java.lang.NullPointerException: marginProfile is null for account' (202), summing exactly to 426.

The full 426/426 ERROR population was assembled by pagination and pattern counts sum exactly to each sub-window total (12:22:20–13:00Z: 82+69=151; 13:00–13:59Z: 121+114=235); no non-FNO order-type pattern appears in any segment. A targeted search for the substring 'equity' in order-service ERROR logs over 11:00–13:59Z returned zero matches.
The first error log is at 2026-03-03T12:12:31Z, matching the 12:12Z metric bucket, and error logs run continuously to 13:58:50Z, so the failure is ongoing, not transient.
The 500s are not a latency/timeout symptom: latency_p99_ms stayed flat ~145–165ms (mean 149.99ms) and cpu_pct flat ~36–43% (mean 40.16%) across the whole window.
order-service shows no resource saturation at onset: db_pool_in_use flat ~13.8–14.3 (mean 14.04, max 15.22) and memory_pct flat ~59–61% (mean 60.08) spanning 11:30–13:50Z.

Total request volume to order-service is flat across the incident (request_rate ~230–235 req/s, mean 232.19, min 205.56, max 255.8), so the ~18.5% error rate is not an artifact of a traffic surge; only the error fraction changed.

No downstream or shared component degrades first: pricing-engine error rate is flat 0.18–0.25%, exchange-gateway flat 0.18–0.26%, payment-service flat ~0.17–0.32%, and ledger-db connections_active flat ~60–63 across the window.

api-gateway shows a concurrent smaller error increase (~0.18–0.23% rising to ~2.06% at 12:10Z and settling ~3.3–3.5%), co-timed with and slightly preceding the order-service spike, consistent with the gateway surfacing the same 5xx responses from POST /v1/orders.

The standard config-change endpoint returned zero config changes on ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka and portfolio-service for 11:00–13:59Z, and the standard deployment endpoint returned zero deployments on ledger-db and portfolio-service in that window.

No separately queryable margin/profile/margin-datastore service exists in the fleet: metrics and logs queries for 'margin-service' returned not_found against the known_services list, which contains no margin-service or profile-store entity.

portfolio-service, the only plausible owner of the marginProfile lookup, is completely flat across 11:30–13:59Z: error_rate every bucket 0.18–0.23% (12:10Z bucket avg 0.22), latency_p99 averaging 161.89–206.25ms with the 12:10Z bucket below the 12:00Z bucket, and logs showing only 24 INFO / 2 WARN routine lines with nothing anomalous straddling 12:10–12:12Z.

Historical precedents for order-500 symptoms have different root causes (HIST-103 external exchange API outage, HIST-110 ledger-db IOPS throttling, HIST-115 connection-pool misconfiguration) and therefore serve as leads only, not as this incident's cause.

order-service exposes no order-type/route dimension in its metrics (available_metrics: cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, request_rate, restarts), so order-type exclusivity is evidenced by logs, not metrics.

assumptions: The 'marginProfile is null' condition is produced by the new code path itself (missing/incorrect handling of F&O accounts) rather than by a pre-existing broken/sparse external data record that the new code merely exposed; the null's provenance was not directly traced.

The deploy/config feeds can be trusted as sufficiently complete for shared datastores; the dependency agent flagged that infra-level changes might not surface there, and no separate infra/ops/maintenance feed exists in the tool namespace, so any such change is not queriably observable.
No rollback was performed during the observation window, so no recovery evidence exists for or against H1.
portfolio-service is the owner of the marginProfile lookup; the dependency graph does not list a margin/profile dependency, so ownership is inferred rather than directly traced.
The failure is exclusively on the F&O (derivatives) order path; this is inferred from logs because order-service metrics carry no order-type dimension.

timeline.event: Only unrelated config change in the fleet: cfg-2101 on notification-service (email.batch_size 200 -> 250). Not related to order placement.

order-service deployed to v2.14.0 (dep-5101): new MarginCheckValidator added to the validation chain, legacy OrderRules.validateMargin() removed. This is the only deployment on any service in the 10:00–13:59Z window.
order-service error rate enters the onset bucket (avg 14.74, up from a 12:00Z baseline avg of 0.22); api-gateway error rate also rises to ~2.06% and peaks at 12:10Z.

First order-service ERROR log: NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.validate(MarginCheckValidator.java:88) with orderType=FNO. Errors continue to 13:58:50Z.
Incident INC-001 [SEV-1] reported by on-call SRE; spike in failed order placements, mostly derivatives orders per support tickets.
Probe of a non-standard margin-related service scope fails with upstream timeout after 3 attempts; no separate margin-datastore entity exists in known_services.

End of observation window: dep-5101 still live with no rollback; 426/426 ERROR logs are NullPointerException/FNO marginProfile-null with zero equity-order failures; all downstream and shared components remain flat.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back order-service from v2.14.0 to the prior release (revert deployment dep-5101) as the immediate mitigation, and confirm POST /v1/orders 500s stop and order-service error_rate returns to its ~0.2% baseline.
recommended_actions.rationale: dep-5101 is the sole change on any component at or before the 12:10–12:12Z onset (F1, F3, F24) and is still live; the failure is an immediate NPE inside the validator it added (F9), with the error onset contained in the 12:10Z bucket after it (F14, F8).

recommended_actions.action: If a full rollback is not feasible, disable/remove the new MarginCheckValidator from the validation chain (or restore OrderRules.validateMargin()) via the order-service configuration/feature flag, then verify errors cease.
recommended_actions.rationale: All 426 ERROR logs originate at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 and the legacy margin validation was removed in the same change, so reverting just this validation path should restore behaviour (F1, F9).

recommended_actions.action: Add a null guard for marginProfile in MarginCheckValidator (handle absent F&O margin profiles explicitly, e.g. fall back to the legacy validation behaviour or return a deterministic 4xx rather than an NPE-driven 500), then re-enable the F&O margin check.
recommended_actions.rationale: The NPE is the direct failure mechanism ('marginProfile is null for account') and removing the legacy check eliminated any fallback for F&O accounts (F9, F1).

recommended_actions.action: Verify the fix under F&O order traffic: confirm order-service error_rate returns to ~0.2%, no NullPointerException at MarginCheckValidator.java:88 appears in logs, and api-gateway error rate returns to baseline.
recommended_actions.rationale: The pre-incident baselines are known (order-service ~0.17–0.29%, api-gateway ~0.18–0.23%), giving a clear verification target (F8, F12).

recommended_actions.action: Add a request-path/order-type dimension (e.g. orderType or route label) to order-service metrics so failures can be attributed by product line without relying on log sampling.
recommended_actions.rationale: order-service exposes no order-type dimension (available_metrics list excludes it), so F&O-vs-equity exclusivity could only be established from logs (F35, F34).

recommended_actions.action: Extend deployment/change gating (canary or staged rollout) for validation-path changes to order-service, plus a pre-deploy null/missing-data test for the marginProfile lookup on F&O accounts.
recommended_actions.rationale: The regression shipped and ran for ~1h49m before remediation, and the failure was specific to a data-shape condition (absent F&O margin profile) that a canary on the derivatives path would have caught (F1, F9, F10).

recommended_actions.action: Instrument the marginProfile lookup source with a null-return / lookup-miss counter and an explicit error signal, so a missing-profile condition is observable at the source in future.
recommended_actions.rationale: No null-return/data-completeness metric exists anywhere in the fleet, which is why the null's provenance could only be inferred and why portfolio-service health had to be judged from generic error_rate/latency/logs (F26, F28, F29).

recommended_actions.action: Add or document an infra/ops change feed covering shared datastores (ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka), since the standard deploy/config endpoints are service-scoped and returned empty for them.
recommended_actions.rationale: The dependency agent flagged that infra-level changes on shared components may not surface in the standard feeds, which is the residual alternative path that could not be fully ruled out (F20, F21, F23).

data_gaps: No infra/ops/maintenance change feed or margin-datastore feed exists among the exposed tools; only service-scoped get_deployments and get_config_changes are available, and those returned empty for ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka and portfolio-service. A deploy-free infra-level change on a shared component at 12:10–12:12Z therefore cannot be directly confirmed or excluded (F20, F21, F23).

The provenance of the null marginProfile is untraced: it is not established whether the new code path fails to retrieve/populate the profile or whether a pre-existing sparse data record is simply dereferenced without a guard. This detail does not change the origin or the fix (both lie in the new validation path from dep-5101) but it lowers confidence.

No component in the fleet is named margin-service or profile-store, so the exact owner of the marginProfile lookup could not be confirmed; portfolio-service is inferred as the candidate, and it shows no degradation, but ownership is not directly proven (F23, F25, F30).

portfolio-service logs are sparse (26 lines in the window, ~1 request-batch sample per 6–10 minutes), so the absence of a null/error log line at 12:10–12:12Z is weak evidence against a brief null-return burst (F29).

order-service metrics have no per-order-type/route dimension and the requests_by_order_type query failed; F&O exclusivity of the failures rests on logs alone, so it could not be independently corroborated by a success-rate-by-type metric (F35, F34).

Every error-log page remained truncated within its sub-window, so the full 426-entry population was assembled from pattern counts that reconcile to each sub-window total rather than from inspecting all lines; a rare non-FNO entry in an unreturned page middle is possible in principle, though the counts argue against it (F32, F33).

Several intended probes were cut off by the tool-call budget: ledger-db slow_queries_per_min (the HIST-110 precedent), redis-cache cpu/memory/hit_ratio/evictions, kafka metrics, exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate/upstream_latency_ms, and a null-filtered portfolio-service log query. No positive dependency signal exists, but silent ledger-db throttling or redis saturation is not mechanically excluded (F17).
No rollback or other remediation occurred within the observation window (dep-5101 rolled_back_at is null), so there is no recovery evidence that would confirm causality by reversibility (F1).
what_would_change_the_conclusion: A fleet-wide or infra-level change (e.g. datastore maintenance/throttling, or a config/deploy on ledger-db, redis-cache, kafka or a margin datastore) timestamped at 12:08–12:12Z, discovered via a feed not queried here, would challenge H1 in favour of H3 or H2.

Evidence that marginProfile was already null or missing for F&O accounts before 12:10Z (e.g. pre-deployment traces or data showing the lookup failing beforehand) would shift the origin toward H2 — a pre-existing data gap merely exposed by dep-5101 — and change the recommended fix.

Non-FNO order types also failing with 500s, or errors appearing in a validator stage that runs before/independently of order type, would show the defect is broader than the F&O margin path and would change the scope of the fix.
A rollback of dep-5101 that fails to stop the 500s (persisting NPEs or errors after revert) would falsify H1 as the sufficient cause.

A degraded-but-non-erroring marginProfile source (e.g. portfolio-service returning nulls while showing flat error_rate/latency, visible only via a null-return counter) would revive H2 and relocate the fix outside order-service.
Evidence that the 12:10Z deploy and 12:12Z onset are coincidental — e.g. error logs beginning before 12:10Z or the deployment being a no-op — would weaken the temporal causal chain that anchors H1.
